==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|rāz}}, {{IPA|en|/ɹeɪz/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-raise.ogg|a=US}} * {{homophones|en|rase|rays|raze|rehs|réis|res}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪz|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|reysen}}, {{m|enm|raisen}}, {{m|enm|reisen}}, from {{der|en|non|reisa||to raise}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*raisijaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*raizijaną||to raise}}, causative form of {{der|en|gem-pro|*rīsaną||to rise}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁rey-||to rise, arise}}. According to Kroonen (2013), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-||to stir, rise}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|rāsian||to explore, examine, research}}, {{cog|ang|rīsan||to seize, carry off}}, {{cog|ang|rǣran||to raise}}. {{doublet|en|rear}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|physical}} To cause to [[rise]]; to [[lift]] or [[elevate]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' your hand if you want to say something; to '''raise''' your walking stick to defend yourself}} #: {{ux|en|the flag was '''raised'''}} ## To form by the accumulation of materials or constituent parts; to build up; to erect. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' a wall, or a heap of stones}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|Isaiah|xxxix|3|passage=I will '''raise''' forts against thee.}} ## To cause something to come to the surface of water. ##: {{ux|en|The ship was '''raised''' ten years after it had sunk.}} ## {{lb|en|nautical}} To cause (the land or any other object) to seem higher by drawing nearer to it. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' Sandy Hook light}} ## To make (bread, etc.) light, as by [[yeast]] or [[leaven]]. ## {{lb|en|figurative}} To cause (a dead person) to live again; to [[resurrect]]. ##: {{ux|en|The magic spell '''raised''' the dead from their graves!}} ## {{lb|en|military}} To remove or break up (a blockade), either by withdrawing the ships or forces employed in enforcing it, or by driving them away or dispersing them. ## {{lb|en|military|transitive}} To relinquish (a [[siege]]), or cause this to be done. ## {{lb|en|metalworking|transitive}} To emboss (sheet metal), or to form it into cup-shaped or hollow articles, by hammering, stamping{{,}} or spinning. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To create, increase or develop. #: {{ux|en|We need to '''raise''' the motivation level in the company.}} #: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' the quality of the products; to '''raise''' the price of goods; to '''raise''' (increase) taxes}} ## To [[collect]] or [[amass]]. ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' a lot of money for charity; to '''raise''' troops}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1955|month=February|author=T. B. Sands|title=The Didcot, Newbury & Southampton Railway—1|journal=Railway Magazine|page=79|text=But capital was proving difficult to '''raise'''; rumours were in the air that the G.W.R. and L.S.W.R. were about to patch up their quarrel, and the people of Southampton, who twelve months earlier had staged a torch-light procession to celebrate the passing of the D.N.S.R. Act, were increasingly loath to part with their cash.}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[call up]] the [[force]]s of, to raise the [[troop]]s from. ##* {{RQ:Jack Straw|III|55|May it pleaſe your Grace that I ſhall '''raiſe''' the ſtreets,
To Gard your Maieſtie through Smithfield as you walke.}} ## To [[bring up]]; to [[grow]]. ##: {{ux|en|We visited a farm where they '''raise''' chickens.}} ##: {{ux|en|Chew with your mouth shut — were you '''raised''' in a barn?}} ##* {{quote-book|en |url=https://archive.org/details/chinaurbanizatio0000unse/ |year=1981 |ISBN=0-231-05076-3 |title=Literature of the Hundred Flowers |volume=II |editor=w:Hualing Nieh |publisher=w:Columbia University Press |page=xxxix |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/literatureofhund0002unse/page/n44/ |text={{w|Ting Ling}} had disappeared from public life in 1958. She was accused of being a "Rightist" and was sent to a farm in Hei-lung-chiang Province in remote northeast China, worked there twelve years '''raising''' chickens, was in prison five years (1970-1975), and began to live in a village in Shansi in 1975.}} ## To [[promote]]. ##: {{syn|en|elevate|empower|uplift|Thesaurus:aggrandize}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''raise''' somebody to office}} ## To [[mention]] (a question, issue) for discussion. ##: {{ux|en|A few important questions were '''raised''' after the attack.}} ##* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Tami Luhby, Eric Bradner and Rene Marsh|title=Federal employees confused, angered by Trump’s offer to quit|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/01/politics/federal-worker-buyout-reaction/index.html|date=2025-02-01|passage=President Donald Trump’s offer to most federal employees to resign now and be paid through September stunned the workers who received it – angering some, confusing many and '''raising''' questions about whether the offer is even legal.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260305053850/https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/01/politics/federal-worker-buyout-reaction/index.html|archivedate=5 March 2026}} ##* {{RQ:Wired|author=Andy Greenberg, Lily Hay Newman|title=SignalGate Isn’t About Signal|url=https://www.wired.com/story/signalgate-isnt-about-signal/|date=2025-03-26|passage=All of which is to say, SignalGate '''raises''' plenty of security, privacy, and legal issues.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260927221948/https://www.wired.com/story/signalgate-isnt-about-signal/|archivedate=27 September 2026}} ## {{lb|en|legal}} To create; to constitute (a ''[[use]]'', or a beneficial interest in property). ##: {{ux|en|There should be some consideration (i.e., payment or exchange) to '''raise''' a use.}} ## To bring into being; to produce; to cause to arise, come forth, or appear. ##: {{ux|en|Starting in January we will '''raise''' (introduce) taxes on all tobacco substitutes and vaping accessories.}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|Deuteronomy|xviii|18|passage=I will '''raise''' them up a prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=10|passage=God voutsafes to raise another World From him [Noah], and all his anger to forget.|year=1873}} ##* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=5|passage=The most rapid and most seductive transition in all human nature is that which attends the palliation of a ravenous appetite.{{...}}Can those harmless but refined fellow-diners be the selfish cads whose gluttony and personal appearance so '''raised''' your contemptuous wrath on your arrival?}} # To establish contact with (e.g., by telephone or radio). #: {{ux|en|Despite all the call congestion, she was eventually able to '''raise''' the police.}} # {{lb|en|poker|intransitive}} To respond to a [[bet]] by increasing the amount required to continue in the hand. #: {{ux|en|John bet, and Julie '''raised''', requiring John to put in more money.}} # {{lb|en|arithmetic}} To [[exponentiate]], to [[involute]]. #: {{ux|en|Two '''raised''' to the fifth power equals 32.}} # {{lb|en|linguistics|transitive|of a verb}} To extract (a [[subject]] or other [[verb]] [[argument]]) out of an inner [[clause]]. # {{lb|en|linguistics|transitive|of a vowel}} To produce a [[vowel]] with the [[tongue]] positioned closer to the [[roof]] of the mouth. # To increase the nominal value of (a cheque, money order, etc.) by fraudulently changing the writing or printing in which the sum payable is specified. # {{lb|en|programming|transitive}} To [[instantiate]] and [[transmit]] (an [[exception]], by [[throw]]ing it, or an [[event]]). #: {{ux|en|A division by zero will '''raise''' an exception.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Bruce Bukovics|title=Pro WF: Windows Workflow in .NET 3.0|page=243 |passage=Provide some mechanism in the local service class to '''raise''' the event. This might take the form of a public method that the host application can invoke to '''raise''' the event.}} # {{lb|en|India|transitive}} To [[open]], [[initiate]]. #: {{ux|en|I will '''raise''' a trouble-ticket in order to correct this reporting issue.}} # {{misspelling of|en|raze}}. =====Usage notes===== * It is standard US English to raise children, and this usage has become common in all kinds of English since the 1700s. Until fairly recently, however, US teachers taught the traditional rule that one should raise crops and animals, but [[rear]] children, despite the fact that this contradicted general usage. It is therefore not surprising that some people still prefer "to rear children" and that this is considered correct but formal in US English. Modern British English also prefers "raise" over "rear". * It is generally considered incorrect to say ''rear crops or (adult) animals'' in US English, but this expression is (or was until relatively recently) common in British English. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|stem=rais|old=1}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|to cause to rise}} {{l|en|lift}}, {{l|en|hike}} =====Derived terms===== {{rfc|en}}
